Some go because their parents expect it, others because ifs what their friends are doing. Then, there’s the belief that a college degree will 27 ensure a good job and high pay.

Some students 28 through four years, attending classes, or skipping (逃课) them as the case may be, reading only what can’t be avoided, looking for less 29 courses, and never being touched or changed in any important way. For a few of these people, college provides no 30 , yet because of parental or peer pressure, they cannot voluntarily leave. They stop trying in the hope that their teachers will make the decision for them by 31 them.

To put it bluntly /(直截了当地）,unless you’re willing to make your college years count, you might be 32 doing something else. Not everyone should attend college, nor should everyone who does attend begin right after high school. Many college students 33 taking a year or so off. A year out in the world helps some people to 34 their priorities and goals. If you’re really going to get something out of going to college, you have to make it mean something, and to do that you must have some idea why you’re there, what you hope to get out of it, and 35 even what you hope to become.

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions：In this section,you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. Essay-Grading Software Offers Professors a Break
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一篇附有十个陈述的文章。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题纸 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。论文评分软件为教授提供了休息的机会

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Imagine taking a college exam, and, instead of handing in a blue book and getting a grade from a professor a few weeks later, clicking the “send” button when you are done and receiving a grade back instantly, your essay scored by a software program. And then, instead of being done with that exam, imagine that the system would immediately let you rewrite the test to try to improve your grade.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 想象一下，参加一次大学考试，不是交一本蓝皮书并在几周后从教授那里得到成绩，而是在完成后单击“发送”按钮并立即收到成绩，而是由软件程序对你的论文进行评分。然后，想象一下系统会立即让您重写测试以尝试提高您的成绩，而不是完成该考试。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) EdX, the nonprofit enterprise founded by Harvard and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) to offer courses on any institution that wants to use it. The software uses artificial intelligence to grade student essays and short written answers, freeing professors for other tasks.

C) The new service will bring the educational consortium����into a growing conflict over the role of automation in education. Although automated grading systems for multiple-choice and true-false tests are now widespread, the use of artificial intelligence technology to grade essay answers has not yet received widespread acceptance by educators and has many critics.

D) Anant Agarwal, an electrical engineer who is president of EdX, predicted that the instant-grading software would be a useful teaching tool, enabling students to take tests and write essays over and over and improve the quality of their answers. He said the technology would offer distinct advantages over the traditional classroom system, where students often wait days or weeks for grades. “There is a huge value in learning with instant feedback,” Dr. Agarwal said. “Students are telling us they learn much better with instant feedback.”
paragraphs.translationZh: D) EdX 总裁、电气工程师 Anant Agarwal 预测，即时评分软件将成为一种有用的教学工具，使学生能够反复参加考试和撰写论文，并提高答案的质量。他表示，与传统的课堂系统相比，这项技术具有明显的优势，在传统的课堂系统中，学生通常需要等待数天或数周才能获得成绩。 “通过即时反馈进行学习具有巨大的价值，”阿加瓦尔博士说。 “学生们告诉我们，通过即时反馈，他们学得更好。”

paragraphs.sourceText: E) But skeptics (怀疑者) the automated system is no match for live teachers. One longtime critic , Les Perelman, has drawn national attention several times for putting together nonsense essays that have fooled software grading programs into giving high marks. He has also been highly critical of studies claiming that the software compares well to human graders.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 但怀疑者（怀疑者）认为自动化系统无法与现场教师相媲美。一位长期的评论家莱斯·佩雷尔曼（Les Perelman）曾多次引起全国关注，因为他整理了一些无意义的文章，愚弄了软件评分程序，给了高分。他还对声称该软件与人类评分者相比效果更好的研究持强烈批评态度。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) He is among a group of educators who last month began circulating a petition (呼吁) opposing automated assessment software. The group, which calls itself Professionals Against Machine Scoring of Student Essays in High-Stakes Assessment, has collected nearly 2,000 signatures, including some from famous people like Noam Chomsky.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 他是上个月开始散发反对自动评估软件请愿书的一群教育工作者之一。该组织自称为“高风险评估中反对学生论文机器评分的专业人士”，已收集了近 2000 个签名，其中包括诺姆·乔姆斯基等名人的签名。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) “Let’s face the realities of automatic essay scoring,” the group’s statement reads in part. “Computers cannot ‘read’. They cannot measure the essentials of effective written communication: accuracy, reasoning, adequacy of evidence, good sense, ethical ( 伦理的) position, convincing argument, meaningful organization, and clarity, among others.
paragraphs.translationZh: G）“让我们面对自动论文评分的现实，”该组织的声明部分写道。 “计算机无法‘阅读’。它们无法衡量有效书面交流的要素：准确性、推理、证据充分性、良好的判断力、道德立场、令人信服的论点、有意义的组织和清晰度等等。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) But EdX expects its software to be adopted widely by schools and universities. It offers free online classes from Harvard, MIT and the University of California-Berkeley; this fall, it will add classes from Wellesley, Georgetown and the University of Texas. In all, 12 universities participate in EdX, which offers certificates for course completion and has said that it plans to continue to expand next year, including adding international schools.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 但 EdX 预计其软件将被学校和大学广泛采用。它提供哈佛大学、麻省理工学院和加州大学伯克利分校的免费在线课程；今年秋天，它将增加韦尔斯利、乔治城和德克萨斯大学的课程。总共有 12 所大学参与了 EdX，该组织提供课程结业证书，并表示计划明年继续扩张，包括增加国际学校。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) The EdX assessment tool requires human teachers, or graders, to first grade 100 essays or essay questions. The system then uses a variety of machine-learning techniques to train itself to be able to grade any number of essays or answers automatically and almost instantly. The software will assign a grade depending on the scoring system created by the teacher, whether it is a letter grade or numerical（数字的）rank.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) EdX 评估工具要求人类教师或评分者对 100 篇论文或论文问题进行一年级。然后，该系统使用各种机器学习技术来训练自己，使其能够几乎立即自动对任意数量的论文或答案进行评分。软件会根据老师创建的评分系统来分配等级，无论是字母等级还是数字等级。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) EdX is not the first to use the automated assessment technology, which dates to early computers in the 1960s. There is now a range of companies offering commercial programs to grade written test answers, and four states—Louisiana, North Dakota, Utah and West Virginia—are using some form of the technology in secondary schools. A fifth, Indiana, has experimented with it. In some cases the software is used as a “second reader,” to check the reliability of the human graders.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) EdX 并不是第一个使用自动评估技术的公司，该技术可以追溯到 20 世纪 60 年代的早期计算机。现在有一系列公司提供商业项目来对笔试答案进行评分，路易斯安那州、北达科他州、犹他州和西弗吉尼亚州这四个州正在中学中使用某种形式的技术。第五个国家印第安纳州已经进行了实验。在某些情况下，该软件被用作“第二阅读器”，以检查人工评分者的可靠性。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) But the growing influence of the EdX consortium to set standards is likely to give the technology a boost. On Tuesday, Stanford announced that it would work with EdX to develop a joint educational system that will make use of the automated assessment technology.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 但 EdX 联盟制定标准的影响力日益增强，可能会推动该技术的发展。周二，斯坦福大学宣布将与 EdX 合作开发一个利用自动评估技术的联合教育系统。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Two start-ups, Coursera and Udacity, recently founded by Stanford faculty members to create “massive open online courses,” or MOOCs, are also committed to automated assessment systems because of the value of instant feedback. “It allows students to get immediate feedback on their work, so that lean turns into a game, with students naturally(吸引) toward resubmitting the work until they get it right,” said Daphne Roller, a computer scientist and a founder of Coursera.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 两家初创公司 Coursera 和 Udacity 最近由斯坦福大学的教员创立，旨在创建“大规模开放在线课程”（MOOC），由于即时反馈的价值，它们也致力于自动化评估系统。计算机科学家、Coursera 创始人达芙妮·罗勒 (Daphne Roller) 表示：“它可以让学生立即获得作业反馈，从而将精益变成一场游戏，学生们自然而然地会重新提交作业，直到他们做对为止。”

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Last year the Hewlett Foundation, a grant-making organization set up by one of the Hewlett- Packard founders and his wife, sponsored two $100,000 prizes aimed at improving software that grades essays and short answers. More than 150 teams entered each category. A winner of one of the Hewlett contests, Vik Paruchuri, was hired by EdX to help design its assessment software.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 去年，惠普基金会（Hewlett-Packard 创始人之一和他的妻子创立的一个资助组织）赞助了两项 10 万美元的奖金，旨在改进论文和简答题评分软件。每个类别都有超过 150 支队伍参赛。 EdX 聘请了 Hewlett 竞赛的获胜者 Vik Paruchuri 来帮助设计其评估软件。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) “One of our focuses is to help kids learn how to think critically,” said Victor Vuchic, a program officer at the Hewlett Foundation. “ It’s probably impossible to do that with multiple-choice tests. The challenge is that this requires human graders, and so they cost a lot more and they take a lot more time. ”
paragraphs.translationZh: N）“我们的重点之一是帮助孩子们学习如何批判性思考，”休利特基金会的项目官员 Victor Vuchic 说。 “通过多项选择测试可能无法做到这一点。挑战在于，这需要人类评分者，因此成本更高，而且需要更多时间。”

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Mark D. Shermis, a professor at the University of Akron in Ohio, supervised the Hewlett Foundation’s contest on automated essay scoring and wrote a paper about the experiment. In his view, the technology—though imperfect—has a place in educational settings.
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 俄亥俄州阿克伦大学教授马克·D·谢尔米斯 (Mark D. Shermis) 监督了休利特基金会的自动作文评分竞赛，并撰写了一篇有关该实验的论文。在他看来，这项技术虽然不完美，但在教育环境中占有一席之地。

paragraphs.sourceText: P. With increasingly large classes, it is impossible for most teachers to give students meaningful feedback on writing assignments, he said. Plus, he noted, critics of the technology have tended to come from the nation’s best universities, where the level of teaching is much better than at most schools. Q. Often they come from very famous institutions where, in fact, they do a much better job of providing feedback than a machine ever could,” Dr. Shermis said. “ There seems to be a lack of appreciation of what is actually going on in the real world.”
paragraphs.translationZh: P. 他说，随着班级规模越来越大，大多数老师不可能给学生关于写作作业的有意义的反馈。此外，他指出，对该技术的批评者往往来自全国最好的大学，这些大学的教学水平比大多数学校要好得多。问：他们通常来自非常著名的机构，事实上，他们在提供反馈方面比机器做得更好，”谢尔米斯博士说。“人们似乎缺乏对现实世界中实际发生的事情的了解。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. Some professionals in education are collecting signatures to voice their opposition to automated essay grading.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 一些教育专业人士正在收集签名，以表达他们对自动论文评分的反对。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. Using software to grade students’ essays saves teachers time for other work.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 使用软件对学生的论文进行评分可以节省教师的其他工作时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. The Hewlett contests aim at improving essay grading software.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 休利特竞赛旨在改进论文评分软件。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. Though the automated grading system is widely used in multiple-choice tests, automated essay grading is still criticized by many educators.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 尽管自动评分系统广泛应用于多项选择题测试，但自动作文评分仍然受到许多教育工作者的批评。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. Some people don’t believe the software grading system can do as good a job as human graders.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 有些人不相信软件评分系统可以像人类评分员一样做得好。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. Critics of automated essay scoring do not seem to know the true realities in less famous universities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 自动论文评分的批评者似乎并不了解不太出名的大学的真实情况。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. Critics argue many important aspects of effective writing cannot be measured by computer rating programs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 批评者认为有效写作的许多重要方面无法通过计算机评级程序来衡量。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. As class size grows, most teachers are unable to give students valuable comments as to how to improve their writing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 随着班级规模的扩大，大多数教师无法就如何提高写作水平向学生提供宝贵的意见。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. The automated assessment technology is sometimes used to double check the work of human graders.
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 自动评估技术有时用于复核人工评分者的工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. Students find instant feedback helps improve their learning considerably.
paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 学生发现即时反馈有助于大大提高他们的学习水平。

paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The endless debate about “work-life balance ’’ often contains a hopeful footnote about stay-at- home dads. If American society and business won5t make it easier on future female leaders who choose to have children, there is still the ray of hope that increasing numbers of full-time fathers will. But based on today’s socioeconomic trends, this hope is, unfortunately, misguided.
paragraphs.translationZh: 关于“工作与生活平衡”的无休无止的争论往往包含着关于全职爸爸的充满希望的脚注。如果美国社会和企业不能让未来选择生孩子的女性领导人变得更容易，那么越来越多的全职父亲仍然抱有一线希望。但不幸的是，根据当今的社会经济趋势，这种希望是错误的。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s true that the number of men who have left work to do their thing as full-time parents has doubled in a decade, but ifs still very small：only 0. 8% of married couples where the stay-at-home father was out of the labor force for a year. Even that percentage is likely inflated by men thrust into their caretaker role by a downsizing. This is simply not a large enough group to reduce the social stigma(污名)and force other adjustments necessary to supporting men in this decision, even if only for a relatively short time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 诚然，十年来，辞去工作岗位全职父母的男性人数增加了一倍，但比例仍然很小：只有 0. 8% 的已婚夫妇中，全职父亲离开劳动力市场一年。即使是这个比例也可能因为裁员而被推入看守角色的男性所夸大。这根本不是一个足够大的群体，不足以减少社会耻辱并迫使其他必要的调整来支持男性做出这一决定，即使只是在相对较短的时间内。

paragraphs.sourceText: Even shorter times away from work for working fathers are already difficult. A study found that 85% of new fathers take some time off after the birth of a child—but for all but a few, it’s a week or two at most. Meanwhile, the average for women who take leave is more than 10 weeks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于职业父亲来说，即使休假时间更短，也已经很困难了。一项研究发现，85% 的新爸爸在孩子出生后会休息一段时间，但除了少数人外，大多数人最多休息一两周。与此同时，女性平均请假时间超过 10 周。

paragraphs.sourceText: Such choices impact who moves up in the organization. While you’re away, someone else is doing your work, making your sales, taking care of your customers. That can’t help you at work. It can only hurt you. Women, of course, face the same issues of returning after a long absence. But with many more women than men choosing to leave the workforce entirely to raise families, returning from an extended parental leave doesn’t raise as many eyebrows as it does for men.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些选择会影响组织中的晋升。当你离开时，其他人正在做你的工作、进行销售、照顾你的客户。这对你的工作没有帮助。它只会伤害你。当然，女性在久别重逢后也面临着同样的问题。但由于选择完全离开工作岗位养家糊口的女性比男性多，延长育儿假后的回归并不像男性那样引起人们的关注。

paragraphs.sourceText: professions were more family-friendly. In the foreseeable future, stay- at-home fathers may make all the difference for individual families, but their presence won’t reduce the numbers of high-potential women who are forced to choose between family and career.
paragraphs.translationZh: 职业对家庭更加友好。在可预见的未来，全职父亲可能会对个别家庭产生重大影响，但他们的存在不会减少被迫在家庭和事业之间做出选择的高潜力女性的数量。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Some of the world’s most significant problems never hit headlines. One example comes from agriculture. Food riots and hunger make news. But the trend lying behind these matters is rarely talked about. This is the decline in the growth in yields of some of the world’s major crops. A new study by the University of Minnesota and McGill University in Montreal looks at where, and how far, this decline is occurring.
paragraphs.translationZh: 世界上一些最重大的问题从未成为头条新闻。农业就是一个例子。粮食骚乱和饥饿成为新闻。但这些问题背后的趋势却很少被谈论。这是世界上一些主要作物产量增长的下降。明尼苏达大学和蒙特利尔麦吉尔大学的一项新研究着眼于这种下降发生的地点和程度。

paragraphs.sourceText: The authors take a vast number of data points for the four most important crops :rice, wheat, com and soyabeans (大豆).They find that on between 24% and 39% of all harvested areas, the improvement in yields that took place before the 1980s slowed down in the 1990s and 2000s.
paragraphs.translationZh: 作者获取了四种最重要作物的大量数据：水稻、小麦、玉米和大豆。他们发现，在所有收获面积的 24% 至 39% 之间，1980 年代之前的产量提高在 1990 年代和 2000 年代放缓。

paragraphs.sourceText: There are two worrying features of the slowdown. One is that it has been particularly sharp in the world’s most (人口多的）countries, India and China. Their ability to feed themselves has been an important source of relative stability both within the countries and on world food markets. That self-sufficiency cannot be taken for granted if yields continue to slow down or reverse.
paragraphs.translationZh: 经济放缓有两个令人担忧的特点。一是，这种情况在世界上人口最多的国家、印度和中国尤其严重。它们养活自己的能力一直是各国内部和世界粮食市场相对稳定的重要来源。如果产量继续放缓或逆转，那么自给自足就不能被认为是理所当然的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Second, yield growth has been lower in wheat and rice than in com and soyabeans. This is problematic because wheat and rice are more important as foods, accounting for around half of all calories consumed. Com and soyabeans are more important as feed grains. The authors note that “we have preferentially focused our crop improvement efforts on feeding animals and cars rather than on crops that feed people and are the basis of food security in much of the world. ”,
paragraphs.translationZh: 其次，小麦和水稻的产量增长低于玉米和大豆。这是有问题的，因为小麦和大米作为食物更重要，约占所有消耗热量的一半。玉米和大豆作为饲料谷物更为重要。作者指出，“我们优先将农作物改良工作的重点放在喂养动物和汽车上，而不是喂养人类的农作物上，而农作物是世界大部分地区粮食安全的基础。”，

paragraphs.sourceText: The report qualifies the more optimistic findings of another new paper which suggests that the world will not have to dig up a lot more land for farming in order to feed 9 billion people in 2050, as the Food and Agriculture Organisation has argued.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该报告证实了另一篇新论文中更为乐观的发现，该论文表明，正如联合国粮食及农业组织所言，到 2050 年，世界将不需要挖掘更多的土地来养活 90 亿人。

paragraphs.sourceText: Instead, it says, thanks to slowing population growth, land currently ploughed up for crops might be able to revert (回返） to forest or wilderness. This could happen. The trouble is that the forecast assumes continued improvements in yields, which may not actually happen.
paragraphs.translationZh: 相反，它说，由于人口增长放缓，目前为农作物而耕种的土地可能会恢复为森林或荒野。这种情况可能会发生。问题在于，预测假设产量持续提高，但实际上可能不会发生。
